Analyse a published administrative table in one call

Source: R/analyse_table.R
anltab.Rd

The questions asked of a published table are always the same: what is in it, what changed between periods and how sure can one be, what the rates are if there is an exposure, whether a short series trends, and whether this release differs from the one held before. Each has a function in this package; this runs them together, with the pieces a reviewer needs and that are easy to forget on a deadline: exact intervals on every change, multiple-comparison adjustment over the groups scanned, the envelope that rounding and suppression in the release imply, and a drift screen against the prior capsule.

Usage

anltab(
  data,
  value,
  prd,
  by = NULL,
  pop = NULL,
  prior = NULL,
  units = c("count", "continuous", "percent"),
  rnd = NULL,
  rndkind = c("nearest", "random"),
  suplim = NULL,
  dir = c("neutral", "higher", "lower"),
  per = 1000,
  conflvl = 0.95,
  alpha = 0.05,
  adjust = "BH",
  prdord = NULL
)

Arguments

data

A data frame in long form: one row per period and group.

value

Name of the column (a string) with the published count (or measure).

prd

Name of the column with the period (fiscal year, quarter, ...); numeric periods are used as the time axis of the trend tests. Text periods ("2019/20", "2021 Q3", "Mar 2021") are ordered as yoy() reads them (see its prd), or as prdord gives.

by

Optional character vector of grouping column names (institution, region, ...). NULL (the default) treats the table as one series.

pop

Optional name of an exposure column for rates (NULL, the default, skips the rate step).

prior

Optional data frame: the previous capsule of the same table, for the drift screen. NULL (the default) skips it.

units

"count" (the default), "continuous" or "percent", as in yoy().

rnd, rndkind, suplim

How the release rounds or suppresses cells; see pubbnd(). rnd is the rounding base (for example 5), rndkind "nearest" (the default) or "random", suplim the threshold below which cells are suppressed. NULL when the counts are exact. Used only for counts: with other units they are ignored, with a warning.

dir

Which way is an improvement, as in yoy(): "neutral" (the default), "higher" or "lower".

per

Rate denominator, as in rtcalc(); default 1000 (rates per 1,000 of pop).

conflvl

Confidence level for every interval, default 0.95.

alpha

Level for the multiple-comparison decision and the drift screens, default 0.05.

adjust

Multiple-comparison method for scanadj(). The default is "BH" (Benjamini-Hochberg).

prdord

Optional character vector: the period labels in order, for text periods the reader does not know (see yoy()); passed to yoy(), ratechg() and the trend tests.

Value

A list of class bricklayer_analysis (with a print method that summarises it in a few lines):

profile

profcols() of data.

missingness

named numeric from misssmry().

change

the yoy() table; for counts with the added columns p_value, padj and significant, and with env_* and compctlo/compctup when publication bounds were requested.

rates, ratechg

the rtcalc() and ratechg() tables when population is given, otherwise NULL.

trend

data frame with one row per group: the by columns, periods, first, last, tau, trndp, slope, rateratio, rateratiolo, rateratioup.

drift

cpsdrft() result against prior, or NULL.

meta

list of the arguments used, nrows, the sorted periods, prior (logical) and when (a time stamp).

Details

The steps, in order:

  1. profile: profcols() and misssmry() on data;

  2. change: yoy() between consecutive periods within each by group. For units = "count" the exact p-values are then adjusted across all comparisons with scanadj(), and, when rnd or suplim is given, yoybnd() adds the publication envelope (see pubbnd()). For "continuous" and "percent" units neither step runs: rnd and suplim are then ignored, with a warning;

  3. rates (only with pop): rtcalc() per group and period, and ratechg() between periods, adjusted with scanadj();

  4. trend: per group, the values summed within each period, then trndtst() (Mann-Kendall tau, p-value and Theil-Sen slope) and, for counts, cnttrnd() (Poisson rate ratio per period). A group with fewer than three periods gets NA; a test that fails gets NA rather than an error;

  5. drift (only with prior): cpsdrft() of data against prior.

Nothing is written and nothing is fetched; a progress bar for the trend step is drawn on stderr unless options(morie.quiet = TRUE). Errors: data or prior not a data frame; a named column not in data; an invalid units, dir or rndkind; a conflvl outside (0, 1); and any error of the functions called (for example negative counts in yoy()).

See also

rptanl() writes the result as a Markdown or HTML report.

Examples

path <- system.file("extdata", "otis_a01_individuals.csv",
                    package = "rmoriebricklayer")
otis <- read.csv(path)
a <- anltab(otis, value = "individuals", prd = "year",
                   by = c("table", "group"))
a
#> ╭── Analysis of a published table ────────────────────────────────────────╮
#> │   Value       `individuals`                                             │
#> │   Period      year                                                      │
#> │   Periods     3 (2023 to 2025)                                          │
#> │   Grouped by  table x group                                             │
#> │   Rows        15                                                        │
#> │   Columns     4                                                         │
#> │   Missing     no missing values                                         │
#> │   Changes     10 comparison(s), 9 significant after BH at 0.05          │
#> │   Trend       0 of 5 series with Mann-Kendall p < 0.05                  │
#> │                                                                         │
#> │   Changes are between consecutive periods with exact or interval tests, │
#> │   adjusted for the number of comparisons; rptanl() writes the full      │
#> │   tables as a report, and x$change, x$rates and x$trend hold them.      │
#> │                                                                         │
#> │   Run 2026-10-29 13:10                                                  │
#> ╰─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
a$change[, c("table", "group", "year", "pctchg", "padj")]
#>           table    group year     pctchg          padj
#> 1  age_category 18 to 24 2023         NA            NA
#> 2  age_category 18 to 24 2024 -16.053607  3.164937e-12
#> 3  age_category 18 to 24 2025  25.271739  1.664477e-19
#> 4  age_category 25 to 49 2023         NA            NA
#> 5  age_category 25 to 49 2024  -3.248493  5.269786e-03
#> 6  age_category 25 to 49 2025  27.947387 3.609584e-109
#> 7  age_category      50+ 2023         NA            NA
#> 8  age_category      50+ 2024  -3.924915  1.794906e-01
#> 9  age_category      50+ 2025  27.664298  6.794641e-18
#> 10       gender   Female 2023         NA            NA
#> 11       gender   Female 2024  27.332892  2.786935e-12
#> 12       gender   Female 2025  46.621622  2.223495e-38
#> 13       gender     Male 2023         NA            NA
#> 14       gender     Male 2024  -8.059159  1.161620e-15
#> 15       gender     Male 2025  25.438844 8.427443e-112
a$trend[, c("group", "tau", "trndp", "rateratio")]
#>      group       tau     trndp rateratio
#> 1 18 to 24 0.3333333 1.0000000  1.027143
#> 2 25 to 49 0.3333333 1.0000000  1.118024
#> 3      50+ 0.3333333 1.0000000  1.112728
#> 4   Female 1.0000000 0.3333333  1.376319
#> 5     Male 0.3333333 1.0000000  1.077781

# counts published rounded to base 5: the intervals widen
b <- anltab(otis, value = "individuals", prd = "year",
                   by = c("table", "group"), rnd = 5)
b$change[1:3, c("group", "year", "pctlo", "compctlo")]
#>      group year     pctlo  compctlo
#> 1 18 to 24 2023        NA        NA
#> 2 18 to 24 2024 -20.09432 -20.09432
#> 3 18 to 24 2025  19.31564  19.31564

# rates with an exposure column
d <- data.frame(year = rep(2019:2022, 2), site = rep(c("A", "B"), each = 4),
                n = c(10, 12, 15, 9, 30, 28, 35, 40),
                pop = rep(c(1000, 2000), each = 4))
r <- anltab(d, "n", "year", by = "site", pop = "pop", per = 1000)
r$ratechg[, c("site", "year", "rate", "rateratio", "padj")]
#> ╭── Change in rate ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
#> │   Rows     8                                                          │
#> │   Columns  5                                                          │
#> │                                                                       │
#> │   site  year   rate  rateratio   padj                                 │
#> │   ----  ----  -----  ---------  -----                                 │
#> │   A     2019  10.00                                                   │
#> │   A     2020  12.00      1.200  0.896                                 │
#> │   A     2021  15.00      1.250  0.896                                 │
#> │   A     2022   9.00      0.600  0.896                                 │
#> │   B     2019  15.00                                                   │
#> │   B     2020  14.00      0.933  0.896                                 │
#> │   B     2021  17.50      1.250  0.896                                 │
#> │   B     2022  20.00      1.143  0.896                                 │
#> │                                                                       │
#> │   Some of this result's columns are not here (a subset of it?), so it │
#> │   is shown as a plain table.                                          │
#> ╰───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯

# a column that is not in the data is an error
try(anltab(otis, value = "count", prd = "year"))
#> Error : anltab: column `count` not found in `data`
